umf.visual.title: A developer's first map of Beacon
umf.visual.question: Where do I start in Beacon, and how is one draft asked for?
umf.visual.takeaway: Start at the API: it is the only part that acts for an agent, and the only part that calls the model gateway.

nodes.label: Sign-in proxy
nodes.detail: checks identity, forwards the agent's token

nodes.label: Beacon API
nodes.detail: every request runs as the agent

edges.label: opens a ticket
edges.why: nothing reaches Beacon without a signed-in agent

edges.label: routes to a model
edges.why: the gateway, not Beacon, chooses and meters the model

edges.label: forwards with the agent's token
edges.why: the API acts as the agent, never as a service account

edges.label: asks for a draft
edges.why: drafting is the only call that leaves the platform's trust boundary

edges.label: audit spans, OTLP
edges.why: every draft and every send is traced back to the agent who asked

steps.title: Opens a ticket
steps.caption: The proxy signs the agent in through the identity provider and keeps their token.

steps.title: Forwards with the agent's token
steps.caption: Every later call carries the agent's identity, so the helpdesk's own permissions still apply.

steps.title: Asks for a draft
steps.caption: The API sends the ticket, its history and the matching articles in one prompt.

steps.title: Routes to a model
steps.caption: Beacon names a purpose, not a model, so the platform can change models without a release.

steps.title: Audit spans, OTLP
steps.caption: Spans carry the ticket and the agent, never the ticket's text.

omissions: This is a conceptual map, not a deployment topology. Left out on purpose, by layer: People (Customer, Workspace admin); Front door (Identity provider); Beacon (Beacon, Web app, Reply drafter, Job worker, Policy rules); Beacon data (Beacon database, Job queue, Attachment store); Neighbours (Helpdesk, Knowledge base); Delivery (CI runner). Not real yet: Policy rules (placeholder), Attachment store (unknown).
